name: neurosurgical emergencies overview
title: Neurosurgical emergencies: headache, coma, a new deficit or trauma mean pressure in a closed skull; protect the airway, image, and decompress according to what takes up the space: an epidural or acute subdural hematoma, a ruptured aneurysm, a tumour with edema, or hydrocephalus

nodes.title: Headache · coma · new neurological deficit · trauma: the cause is PRESSURE
lines: examine to LOCALIZE: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), PUPILS, cranial nerves, pronator drift, power side to side, sensory level
"GCS 15, moving x 4" can hide 1/5 hand intrinsics + 0/5 legs = T1 cord injury · E1 V3 M5, right arm weaker, ICP 20 = brain injury
INTUBATE for GCS < 9 (airway protection) → image → emergency neurosurgery = DECOMPRESSION

nodes.title: BLOOD
lines: which space it is in decides the shape and the outlook

nodes.title: A MASS
lines: weeks of progressive deficit

nodes.title: TRAPPED CSF
lines: the brain squeezed from inside

nodes.title: Epidural hematoma
lines: middle meningeal ARTERY
contact blow to the side of the head

nodes.title: Acute subdural hematoma
lines: BRIDGING VEINS
acceleration-deceleration

nodes.title: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
lines: ruptured ANEURYSM

nodes.title: Tumour with edema
lines: leaky tumour vessels: VASOGENIC edema

nodes.title: Hydrocephalus
lines: e.g. after bacterial meningitis

nodes.title: LUCID interval, then coma
lines: • stunned, then fine, then cannot be woken
• BLOWN PUPIL on the SAME side (third nerve)
• opposite side weaker
case: 24 y, baseball to the right head · played on · unrousable 4 h later · E3 V3 M5, right pupil 4 mm vs 3 mm, left weaker

nodes.title: Falling consciousness
lines: • intoxicated, on ASA
• fixed dilated pupil, posturing
case: 54 y, rolled + ejected, drunk, ASA 325 mg · E1 VT M3, extends left, flexes right · right pupil fixed 5 mm

nodes.title: Explosive headache UNLIKE ANY OTHER
lines: • vomiting, photophobia
• stiff neck, retinal hemorrhage
• GCS may be 15
case: 43 y, a migraineur · bat to the back of the head · BP 160/90, normal exam

nodes.title: Weeks of progressive deficit
lines: • word-finding, one weak hand
• then a rapid fall in consciousness
case: 69 y, 4 weeks word-finding, slurred, drops cup in right hand · 12 h decline · E1 V2 M4

nodes.title: Not rousable
lines: • dysconjugate gaze
• fever if infection
case: 14 y, 48 h malaise, fever · E3 V4 M5, pupils 4 mm reactive

nodes.title: CT: blood in the subarachnoid space
lines: lumbar puncture: blood in the CSF

nodes.title: Enlarged ventricles
lines: cloudy CSF = bacterial meningitis

nodes.title: EARLY decompression
lines: • emergency burr hole (case: right)
• predictably good results: normal in 48 h

nodes.title: Evacuate the hematoma
lines: outcome UNPREDICTABLE: depends on the brain injury underneath

nodes.title: EARLY aneurysm repair
lines: • one bleed: 50% DIE, 75% disabled
• re-rupture 6% day 1, 20% at 2 weeks, 50% at 6 months
• protects against the NEXT bleed only
• outcome follows the PRESENTING neurological state

nodes.title: DEXAMETHASONE 10 mg IV
lines: restores the blood-brain barrier → edema shrinks

nodes.title: + MANNITOL 20% IV push (300 cc)
lines: shrinks brain with an INTACT barrier

nodes.title: Resect once stable
lines: case: GCS 15 again → resected at 72 h

nodes.title: DIVERT the CSF: untreated it KILLS by herniation
lines: • now: EXTERNAL VENTRICULAR DRAIN (case: GCS 14 in 4 h)
• long term: ventriculoperitoneal SHUNT
• treat the cause (antibiotics)
